{{Short description|Chinese physicist (1920–2013)}}
{{family name hatnote|[[Xu (surname 許)|Xu]]|lang=Chinese}}

'''Xu Liangying''' ({{zh|t=許良英 |s=许良英}}; 3 May 1920 – 28 January 2013) was a Chinese [[physicist]], [[translator]] and a [[historian]] and [[philosopher]] of [[natural science]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rue89.com/2013/01/28/mort-de-xu-liangying-92-ans-savant-chinois-et-dissident-toute-sa-vie-239060 |title=Mort de Xu Liangying, 92 ans, savant chinois et dissident toute sa vie &#124; Une Vigie Rue89 |language=fr |publisher=Rue89.com |access-date=2013-01-28}}</ref>

==Biography==
Xu was born in [[Linhai]] of [[Taizhou, Zhejiang|Taizhou]], [[Zhejiang]] on May 3 of 1920. Xu graduated from the Department of Physics of [[Zhejiang University]] in 1942. Xu was a student of [[Shu Xingbei]] and [[Wang Ganchang]].

Xu was an editor of ''Chinese Science Bulletin'' ({{lang|zh|科学通报}}), a major Chinese science journal. Xu was treated unfairly during [[Mao Zedong]]'s [[Anti-Rightist Campaign]] which started in 1957, and he was sent back to his hometown to undergo "[[reform through labour]]" (laogai). After the end of the [[Cultural Revolution]], Xu was politically rehabilitated and returned to work in [[Beijing]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/08/22/science/22prof.html?pagewanted=all|title=Einstein's Man in Beijing: A Rebel with a Cause|newspaper=The New York Times|date=22 August 2006|last1=Overbye|first1=Dennis}}</ref>

Xu was a longtime researcher at the Institute for the History of Natural Science, [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] ({{lang|zh|中国科学院自然科学史研究所}}).

==Work==
Xu's main interests were in the [[history of science]], the [[philosophy of science]] (especially of [[physics]]), and the relations between science and [[human society]]. Xu's ''The Collected Works of Albert Einstein'' ({{lang|zh|《爱因斯坦文集》}}) currently is the most comprehensive Chinese translational version of [[Albert Einstein]]'s work.<ref>China.com.cn Book Reviews: [http://www.china.com.cn/international/txt/2008-04/18/content_14976106.htm 爱因斯坦文集：一部对中国人影响超常的科学家著作]</ref>

==Award==
Xu received the second [[Andrei Sakharov Prize (APS)|Andrei Sakharov Prize]], from the [[American Physical Society]] (APS) in 2008.<ref>APS: [http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/sakharov.cfm Andrei Sakharov Prize]</ref>
